prerequisites: Basic knowledge of mathematics, mechanics, chemistry, and statistics.

learning_outcomes.text: Become familiar with the design process for civil engineering purposes, building upon and complementing the knowledge and insights already acquired in other courses of the Civil Engineering major.
Work on two design assignments: one at the material level and one at the structural level.
Become acquainted with the various application areas of civil engineering through seminars and visits.
Develop skills in group work and oral/written reporting.
Gain insight into the complexity of the civil engineering design process.
Learn how to think and act conceptually, integratively, and interdisciplinarily.
Gain experience in searching for and processing literature and scientific information.
Learn to collect and process experimental data.
Refine skills in group work and oral/written reporting.

syllabus_topics: Structural design, with a perspective on designing load-bearing structures for buildings and/or infrastructure.
Exploratory design of a small-scale structure.
Final design of a large-scale structure.
Theoretical design of structures.
Construction and functional evaluation of structures.
Influence of design choices on the load-bearing capacity of the structure.
Practical feasibility of the proposed design.
Design of the structure, including mechanical evaluation of its components.
Construction and evaluation of the structure, with attention to deviations between design and performance.
Design of the structure, building on lessons from the first cycle.
Construction and evaluation of the structure, with attention to coordinated execution.
Fundamental concepts of designing a construction component for buildings and/or infrastructure.
Application of concepts to a reinforced concrete beam.
Design of a concrete beam based on group-specific boundary conditions (e.g., load combinations, environmental class, basic concrete property requirements).
Creation of concrete test specimens.
Testing of concrete properties.
Design of a test setup for a load test on the concrete beam.
Statistical analysis of test results.
Application of basic concepts for designing a concrete beam.
Understanding basic principles for determining concrete properties and testing a concrete beam through analysis of Eurocodes and test procedures.
Design phase: Concrete composition based on environmental class (NBN EN 206-1 and NBN B15-001), load combinations, Eurocode 2 analysis, reinforced concrete beam design.
Test phase: Test procedures, measurement techniques, beam test setup design, concrete specimen creation, concrete property testing, concrete beam testing and measurement.
Analysis phase: Evaluation and statistical analysis of test results.
Introduction to different specialties within civil engineering, specifically the three possible master options: 'structural engineering', 'hydraulic engineering', and 'building technology'.
Site/company visits covering both design and execution aspects of civil engineering practice.

assessment_methods.method: Structures component (reports, presentations, demonstrations, and/or cooperation)
Materials component (reports, presentations, demonstrations, and/or cooperation)
Seminars component (reports, presentations, demonstrations, and/or cooperation)

assessment_rules: The final score is a weighted average of the scores on the different learning activities: Structures (60%), Materials (35%), and Seminars (5%). There is a correction of max. +/- 2 points based on peer assessment. To pass, a minimum of 40% of the maximum score must be achieved for each learning activity. If this is not met, the maximum achievable score for the course is 9/20. Technical-scientific quality of the final result is always decisive. No resit exam is organized for students who were not active or contributed only partially during the academic year. For students with sufficient contribution, alternative arrangements for shortcomings will be considered.
